# /crav1-design-architecture

lane: cross-cutting | group: Specify | starter: no | stage: preview | since: 1.181.0 | prompts: 2
purpose: Work out an architecture change with the user, one decision at a time, in a sandbox until go-ahead.
use_when: You want to decide how the architecture should change
prompt_note: One framing card for a new or changed goal, then one card per decision, plus at most 3 narrowing questions per decision when ask-me is picked. One decision per round. No cap on how many decisions a session may settle.
reads: Reads `docs/architecture/spec.md` and `left-out.md`, `docs/system/` notes and ADRs, environment, infrastructure and hosting docs, research notes with their stale marks, slice specs when the ask touches one, saved data models when it touches data, code and config in the linked repos, and its own sandbox.
writes: Before go-ahead only `docs/architecture/designs/<topic>/` through `scripts/design_run.py`: `goal.md`, `compare.md`, and per design `design.md`, `questions.md`, `diagrams.md`, `adr/`, and `stages.md` once staged; a one-off file under `_compare/` only when asked. At go-ahead, after the review is fixed or accepted: one block under `## Decided, not built yet` and still-open questions in `docs/architecture/spec.md`, accepted ADR copies in `docs/system/adr/` or `docs/specs/<slug>/adr/`, and the affected diagram.
leaves alone: Leaves `## Confirmed`, `## Accepted from a guess`, `## How the repos connect`, `left-out.md`, requirements, plans, tasks, verify, research notes, question mark lines, application code, pipelines, and live infrastructure alone. Does not commit, push, merge, tag, or open a pull request.
limits: A run without the user never settles a decision, stages, or gives go-ahead. A choice that reverses an accepted ADR, a constraint, or a current environment fact needs a separate yes. A requirement is routed to `/crav1-add-to-spec`.
flow:
- when a slice needs both a UI design and an architecture design, `/crav1-design-ui` runs first.
- `/crav1-design-architecture` (1.181.0, preview) decides how the landscape should change: systems and services and how they connect, environments, infrastructure and hosting, data flows, integrations, and deployment.
- The sandbox is `docs/architecture/designs/<topic>/` on its own design branch: one goal per topic in `goal.md`, one or more designs under `designs/<name>/`, and `compare.md` once a topic fans out.
- The end state is designed first; staging happens only on `stage-it`, and the user names and divides the stages.
- No other skill reads the sandbox, even after it is merged (except `/crav1-explain-tech`, which only lists mentions read-only and calls them not decided, 1.192.0).
- The skill's `scripts/design_run.py` owns the folder format and every move, saves after each one, and refuses writes outside the topic folder before go-ahead.
- At go-ahead the chosen design is reviewed, then copied as one block under `## Decided, not built yet` in `docs/architecture/spec.md` with a "Designed in" link, its draft ADRs are copied as accepted, and still-open questions go into that spec.
- `change-goal` changes an open topic's goal in place: `design_run.py change-goal --topic <t> --input <json> --reason "<why>"` shows old and new without writing, then with `--yes` rewrites `goal.md` and logs the date, the reason and each change under `## Goal changes`.
- Decisions can be added, dropped, renamed or reordered; a dropped decision stays, marked `dropped` with its reason.
- A settled or leaning decision that is renamed, listed under `reopen`, or names a word from a removed constraint, criterion or driver is marked reopened for another look.
- `create --topic <t> --builds-on <base>` records `Builds on: <base>`, lists the base's settled decisions as fixed inputs, and cuts the design branch from `design/<base>` (updates by `git merge design/<base>`, never a rebase).
- `resume` names decisions the base settled or reopened since the last run, a local change of a base decision is refused with a `revisit` that reopens it in the base topic, `status` shows links both ways, and `go-ahead` on the linked topic waits until the base design is in the architecture spec on main, with a Waiting line naming the base pull request.
- decisions and open questions keep the order they were added (or the goal's order after `change-goal`), and `resume` takes the first reopened, then the first open big decision, then detail decisions (`{"title": ..., "detail": true}`).
- `ending` prints one `Waiting:` line per list item and reads `uncommitted` as a count, a list of paths, true or text.
- `lean` matches short driver names to listed drivers.
- Cards hold at most 4 options and one question, typed input goes through Other, and an empty Other is asked again; kit-lint checks this skill's cards.
- input files go in `docs/architecture/designs/<topic>/inputs/` (an input outside the specs repo is refused), `note` appends scans, visions, scope lists and answers to the topic's `notes.md` (allowed in prepare, used before parking), `create` and `change-goal` refuse unknown keys by name and save a `notes` key with note, `create` creates or checks `design/<topic>` (from `design/<base>` for a linked topic), a move on the wrong branch names `git switch design/<topic>`, `small-fix` lists changes with no design choice that go-ahead copies with no ADR, and Step 1 reads plans, tasks and build maps so planned work is not proposed again.
- design branch update: resume and every move that starts work on a topic fetch and check whether `design/<topic>` is behind `origin/main` (and `design/<base>` for a linked topic), and offer `git merge --no-ff` on a yes card through `branch-behind --topic <t> --yes`; never a rebase, a conflict merges nothing and names the files, and a run without the user never merges.
- base to linked update: after a committed change to a base topic, the ending lists linked topics whose `design/<linked>` is behind `design/<base>`, and one yes card runs `linked-behind --topic <base> --yes`: switch, `git merge --no-ff design/<base>`, switch back; a conflict stops on that branch, names the files and leaves the rest; a run without the user merges nothing.
- `design.md` stores decisions by title so parallel adds do not conflict, and each decision has `Order: N` for the index and resume (ties by title); the goal's decision list comes from those numbers and older files get them on read.
- A move on the wrong branch offers a yes card and `switch-branch --topic <t> --yes` switches itself (refused, naming the paths, on a dirty tree).
- `resume` offers `change-goal` for a saved goal file in `inputs/` not yet applied and never recreates a topic, and returns `kit_check` when the stated kit version and the skill files differ (offering `/crav1-update-kit`); a branch whose kit is behind origin/main gets the merge card before the topic is touched.
- scratch input (ending state, lean, settle, stage and compare drafts) goes in the session's temp folder and is refused from `inputs/`, which holds only the user's saved goal files and is created on the first save for older topics.
- `uncommitted` is a count (`true` is counted from git status), a commit card (`commit --topic <t> --yes`) comes before the ending, `create --builds-on` refuses while the base topic is uncommitted, and the ending prints the routable `/crav1-design-architecture builds-on <base> <idea>`.
- the design branch check, the kit-behind check and the go-ahead base check use the repo's default branch (`origin/HEAD`, else `origin/main`, then `origin/master`), skip with a reason when there is none, and name that branch in cards and Run next.
- next is the guided card.
- A proposal page and a briefing share one decisions section, stage numbers start at 1, and a routed requirement names the slice and the text.
- `settle-preview` recommends one by one and settles nothing; there is no settle batch.
- `stop and commit` is a commit yes only when this skill says so.
- A topic whose goal is only on `design/<topic>` offers the switch card.
- `resume --json` leaves Status as it is, including parked; a source that changed still marks that decision reopened.
- Dated pages under `docs/architecture/proposals/` count as the proposal.
- Waiting lines name each person once, with the date on the question, near 120 characters.
- An ended screen's one command is `reopen`.

## Choice words
- question: Which step
  - `resume`: Alias of the status screen. Same text as starting fresh, for the same files. Does not change the session.
  - `next`: Open the guided card for the next decision. Cards appear only from this word.
  - `park`: Park the session. Prints Session parked and the plain command to open it again.
  - `end`: End the session. Prints Session ended and the plain command to open it again.
  - `reopen`: Open an ended session again and print the status screen.
  - `status`: Show open topics, designs, decisions, stages and questions. Writes nothing.
  - `fan-out`: Start a competing design under the same goal, as a copy or from a blank start.
  - `stage-it`: Suggest a split of the designed end state into stages that the user names and divides.
  - `go-ahead`: Review the chosen design, then copy it into the architecture spec after the findings are fixed or accepted.
  - `compare-topics`: One-off comparison of designs from different topics, with criteria the user picks.
  - `prepare`: Gather facts, draft options with recommendations, and refresh comparisons. Settles nothing.
  - `change-goal`: Change an open topic's goal in place after a card shows old and new, with a dated log; touched settled decisions get another look.
  - `builds-on`: Start a topic that builds on an existing one; the base topic's settled decisions are fixed inputs.
  - `note`: Save discussion that is not a decision yet (a scan, a vision, a scope list, answers) into the topic's notes.md.
  - `small-fix`: Record a change that needs no design choice; it is copied at go-ahead with no ADR.
  note: With or without a topic, and with or without resume, the start is the status screen. next opens the guided card. A run without the user is always prepare. Per-decision reply words: choose-a, choose-b, choose-c, choose-mine, discuss, add-my-idea, ask-me, to-question, to-research, skip-for-now.
called_by: Called by the user. `/crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build` may offer it.
runs by itself: Calls no skill. It may name `/crav1-tighten-spec`, `/crav1-plan-from-spec`, `/crav1-add-to-spec`, and `/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions`.
you run next: /crav1-tighten-spec; /crav1-plan-from-spec; /crav1-add-to-spec; /crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions
